official_sources.title: LIDAR DTM Time Stamped Tiles
official_sources.finding: The Environment Agency time-stamped DTM archive contains survey-specific raster terrain products at 25cm, 50cm, 1m and 2m; GeoTIFF data is distributed in 5km zipfiles, in metres, referenced to Ordnance Survey Newlyn and aligned to the OS Grid. The metadata index catalogue identifies available survey dates, product resolution, transformation and geoidal model for a location.
official_sources.limitation: Dataset-level accuracy and metadata do not identify the exact target parcel survey without querying and binding the location-specific metadata index.

official_sources.title: LIDAR Time Stamped Point Cloud
official_sources.finding: The point-cloud archive supplies x,y,z points and attributes; time-stamped DTM/DSM rasters are derived from point clouds, but historic archiving means a matching point cloud may not exist for every surface model. Ground-classified points can differ from the final DTM because the derived terrain model receives further manual editing. Coverage metadata provides survey start/end flown dates and attributes such as average point density.
official_sources.limitation: Point-cloud ground points are diagnostic evidence and cannot silently replace the final authoritative DTM raster.

official_sources.title: National LIDAR Programme
official_sources.finding: The National LIDAR Programme divided England into 302 Phase 1 survey blocks captured mainly in winter between January 2017 and February 2023. Repeat surveys receive incrementing phase numbers for that block and are commissioned according to need rather than a complete rolling national recapture.
official_sources.limitation: A phase number identifies repeat lineage within a block but must still be bound to the exact block, survey dates and target location.

official_sources.title: LIDAR Composite DTM 1m
official_sources.authority: Environment Agency / Defra Data Services Platform
official_sources.finding: The 2022 1m composite combines Time Stamped archive and National LIDAR Programme surveys; where repeats exist the newest, best-resolution data is used and resampled data uses bilinear interpolation. The composite contains surveys from 6 June 2000 to 2 April 2022, and the metadata survey index identifies which survey contributed at a location.
official_sources.limitation: Composite publication year is not the acquisition date of every cell; per-location survey lineage must be resolved through the index.

official_sources.title: LIDAR Composite DTM 2m
official_sources.authority: Environment Agency / Defra Data Services Platform
official_sources.finding: The 2022 2m composite merges and may resample Time Stamped and National LIDAR Programme sources; repeat coverage uses the newest, best-resolution data. Its survey index is explicitly the location-level provenance source for the survey used in the composite.
official_sources.limitation: The composite is derived and may mix surveys of different acquisition dates across adjacent cells or tiles.

official_sources.title: LIDAR Composite DTM 10m
official_sources.finding: The 10m DTM is resampled from the 2m composite using bilinear interpolation and therefore represents an additional derived-resolution layer above the already composited survey lineage.
official_sources.limitation: A 10m bilinear product is unsuitable as terminal evidence when exact native higher-resolution elevation cells are required.

official_sources.title: LIDAR DSM Time Stamped Tiles
official_sources.finding: Time-stamped DSM rasters preserve survey-specific surface elevations including buildings, vegetation and vehicles, while retaining survey-period transformation context and the same OS-grid/OS-Newlyn style of publication.
official_sources.limitation: DSM is not terrain-only DTM and must not be substituted for ground elevation.

official_sources.title: DTM Time Stamped Tiles metadata platform record
official_sources.authority: Environment Agency / Defra Data Services Platform
official_sources.finding: The official platform record exposes EPSG:27700, a dataset period extending through April 2024, related point-cloud/DSM/composite datasets and the published vertical-accuracy statement, reinforcing that transformation/date metadata belongs to the survey product lineage.
official_sources.limitation: Dataset period bounds do not prove the exact survey date at the target location.

official_sources.title: Point Cloud metadata platform record
official_sources.authority: Environment Agency / Defra Data Services Platform
official_sources.finding: The official point-cloud record reiterates that raster DTM/DSM products are derived from the point cloud and that final DTM editing can make classified ground points differ from the final terrain model.
official_sources.limitation: Point-cloud correspondence is not guaranteed for historic surface-model products.

official_sources.title: National LIDAR Programme platform record
official_sources.authority: Environment Agency / Defra Data Services Platform
official_sources.finding: The platform exposes downloadable coverage metadata and repeats the block/phase model: Phase 1 national coverage followed by requirement-driven repeat phases. This provides an official index path for binding target locations to specific programme survey blocks.
official_sources.limitation: Block coverage metadata still needs exact geometry intersection and date-field readback for the target parcel.

official_sources.title: LIDAR Composite DTM 2020 1m retired lineage
official_sources.finding: The retired 2020 1m composite documents the same newest/best-resolution merge rule and states its survey index identifies the Time Stamped survey or National LIDAR Programme block used at a specific location.
official_sources.limitation: Retired composite generations are historical provenance references, not preferred current terminal datasets.

official_sources.title: LIDAR Composite DTM 2020 2m retired lineage
official_sources.finding: The retired 2020 2m composite spans surveys through 1 September 2020 and explicitly instructs users to consult survey-index files to identify the contributing Time Stamped survey or National LIDAR Programme block per location.
official_sources.limitation: Historical composite lineage can validate evolution but should not override a newer authoritative source policy.

official_sources.title: LIDAR Composite DTM 2019 1m retired lineage
official_sources.finding: The retired 2019 1m composite spans surveys through 1 September 2019 and exposes the same survey-index concept for determining which Time Stamped survey or National LIDAR Programme block contributed to a location.
official_sources.limitation: It is retired and is used only to test lineage/version drift, not as the default target source.

official_sources.title: LIDAR Composite DTM 2019 2m retired lineage
official_sources.finding: The 2019 2m composite documents an older survey-date envelope and the same newest/best-resolution composition policy, making it useful for detecting accidental binding to superseded composite generations.
official_sources.limitation: Retired products are not accepted as current terminal evidence without an explicit historical-use requirement.

official_sources.title: LIDAR Composite DTM 2017 25cm retired product
official_sources.finding: The Environment Agency states that the 25cm composite was retired and is no longer produced, while the 25cm time-stamped archive remains available. This separates historical high-resolution survey data from a retired composite product.
official_sources.limitation: Nominally finer resolution does not make a retired composite preferable to correctly dated current survey products.

official_sources.title: LIDAR Composite DSM 1m
official_sources.authority: Environment Agency / Defra Data Services Platform
official_sources.finding: The 1m composite DSM uses similar Time Stamped/National LIDAR Programme survey lineage and index services but contains surface objects, providing a strong product-type guard against accidentally selecting DSM when terrain DTM is required.
official_sources.limitation: DSM lineage may be useful for cross-checking survey identity but its elevations cannot become terrain extrema.
